brief.headline: Press for 30-day extension (freeing ₹53.19 L) by highlighting their 51d payables vs 40d peer median — then offer faster payment for a modest price cut given their thin 2.3% margin.

priceAsk.summary: Benchmark laminate pricing against BOPET film import unit value and offer early payment in exchange for a discount.
priceAsk.basis: Market line for BOPET film — import unit value — is 171.60 ₹/kg. Use this to anchor laminate cost discussions. Given their 2.3% net margin vs 2.5% peer median, avoid aggressive price cuts that risk supply stability; instead, trade faster payment for a modest concession.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Push for 60 Days After Receipt (30-day extension) to free working capital; use their own stretched payables as justification.

brief.financialLeverage: Shrinath's 2.3% net margin sits just below the 2.5% peer median, and their 7.8% EBITDA margin leaves little pricing headroom. However, they already stretch their own suppliers to 51d payable days vs the 40d peer median, so a 30-day extension on our side is defensible. Their debt/equity stands at 1.25x with interest coverage of 1.94x — not distressed, but geared enough to value cash. Our ₹6.47 Cr spend is 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue, so we're a small customer with limited direct leverage. The CARE BBB+ / Stable rating and EPF payment delays flag modest continuity risk, so don't over-squeeze on price.

evidence.point: Their payable days run 11 days longer than peers, so they already stretch their own suppliers.
Their cash-conversion cycle is 37 days longer than the peer median, meaning cash is tied up for over three months.
Net margin is slim and slightly trails peers.
They carry meaningful debt with moderate interest coverage.
We represent less than one percent of their revenue, limiting our direct volume leverage.
BOPET film import unit value provides a market benchmark for laminate raw material.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already in our vendor base — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant covering both film substrate and conversion — can second-source at scale.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specializing in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source option.

risks: CARE BBB+ / Stable rating and EPF payment delays signal modest financial stress — monitor supply continuity if we push too hard.
Their 2.3% net margin leaves little room for deep price cuts without risking their stability and our supply.
Our ₹6.47 Cr spend is only 0.61% of their revenue, so we lack the volume muscle to dictate terms unilaterally.
Debt/equity of 1.25x and interest coverage of 1.94x mean they're leveraged but not distressed — they value cash but aren't desperate.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to discuss extending payment terms to 60 days — your own payables run at 51 days, eleven days longer than the peer median, so this brings us closer to industry practice while freeing up ₹53.19 L in working capital for us.
